subject: Deckard Systems — post-demo: latency budget, token ceiling & hedges
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Liu <alex.liu@deckardsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deckard Systems — post-demo: latency budget, token ceiling & hedges

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposal for next steps so we can size the POC properly.

Key constraints you mentioned on the call:
- Primary SLO: 95th percentile latency target of <= 150ms for single-turn responses under steady-state traffic.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline 120 qps, expected peak burst to 220 qps during business hours.
- Streaming: some user flows (live summary) must stream partial tokens within 60–80ms first-byte when output is >= 512 tokens.
- Context window: central search→answer flow passes 12k tokens of retrieved context (input) and expects ~2k output in the top-quality path.

Implications we discussed:
- 14k token footprint (12k in + 2k out) pushes us into higher compute and latency regimes on most 8/16GB GPU configs; without hedges we'd likely miss 150ms p95.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for users; it doesn't always reduce total CPU, but it helps first-byte SLOs.
- Concurrency bumps require reserved capacity or aggressive batching and shard isolation to avoid tail amplification.

Suggested hedges / options for the POC (we can pick 2–3 to implement as part of the run):
1) Prefix summarization: run a fast extractive summarizer to compress retrieved context to ~2–3k tokens before generation.
2) KV cache for repeated context across queries (you indicated a lot of repeated doc headers).
3) Asynchronous streaming + early partial output for flows where users accept progressive answers.
4) Quantized medium-size model (8-bit) as fallback for non-critical traffic to preserve capacity during bursts.
5) Circuit-breaker: degrade to a smaller context window with a short rationale message when system is over capacity.

Attachments: I attached a short perf-profile baseline (deckard-perf-profile.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (deckard-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with milestones and acceptance criteria.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm top 2 hedges you want exercised in the POC (summarization and KV cache are my recommendation).
- We schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra lead and our runtime engineer (30–45m) to validate metrics we need (token distribution, session stickiness, allowed fallbacks).
- We run a 2-week perf POC with reserved capacity mirroring your peak shaping (we'll provide a canary config and monitoring dashboard).

If that sounds good I can send a calendar invite for the deep-dive; otherwise propose edits to the plan.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (555) 312-8874

From: Alex Liu <alex.liu@deckardsys.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@deckardsys.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deckard Systems — post-demo: latency budget, token ceiling & hedges

Michael — thanks for the clear write-up. That matches our takeaways. Quick answers: 

- We'll prioritize the extractive summarization hedge + KV cache. Our content has a lot of repeated boilerplate sections, so KV cache should buy us meaningful savings.
- Streaming is desirable for our live summarizer UI; first-byte within 80ms is a hard constraint for that product team.
- For the POC scope: start with 120 qps baseline, validate up to 220 qps bursts. If you can show 150ms p95 with summarization + KV cache at baseline, we can evaluate trading quality for cost at bursts.

I'll loop our infra lead Samir into the technical deep-dive — Samir, I'll let you coordinate availability with Michael.

One question on instrumentation: what exact metrics do you need from our side? I'll ask Samir to pull token distribution samples and some example sessions before the call.

—Alex
Alex Liu | Head of AI Product, Deckard Systems
alex.liu@deckardsys.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Deckard Systems — post-demo: latency budget, token ceiling & hedges

Michael — a couple operational notes before the deep-dive: 

1) Capacity sizing: if they want streaming + 2 hedges active, recommend we propose a dedicated pool sized to ~1.5x baseline (so 180 qps steady, 330 qps burst headroom) for the POC. That gives us headroom for A/Bing quantized fallback paths.
2) Metrics checklist to request from Deckard (ask Samir to provide pre-call):
   - Token length histogram (per request): median / 90th / 99th for input and output
   - Fraction of sessions with repeat context (to estimate KV cache hit rate)
   - Distribution of streaming-enabled flows and typical first-chunk size
   - Expected acceptable latency for each UI flow (they gave 80ms first-byte for live summarizer; confirm others)
3) On fallback behavior: draft the copy for the rationale message when we trim context (short sentence to user explaining quality tradeoff). We should prepare an example.

I'll prep the perf runbook and a short checklist for the tech call. Want me to attach the runbook to the hubspot record now or wait for Alex to share token histograms?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
